newsitem.title: UK: Russia maps out investor roadshow for dollar bond.
newsitem.headline: Russia maps out investor roadshow for dollar bond.

text.p: Russia on Wednesday announced the dates of a series of economic presentations to investors ahead of the launch of its third bond issue on international markets.

The Ministry of Finance of the Russian Federation said in a statement that a delegation led by deputy finance minister Mikhail Kasyanov would begin a global roadshow in Seoul on June 11, ending in New York on June 18.
The full programme is as follows:
Kasyanov said on Tuesday that Russia planned to issue its next dollar-denominated Eurobond in the second half of June.
The deal will have a maturity of at least seven years and be jointly arranged by J.P. Morgan and SBC Warburg, he said.
"The volume of the forthcoming issue will be comparable with the established practice," Kasyanov said.
Modern Russia made its debut in the international capital markets last November with a $1 billion five-year Eurobond priced to yield 345 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
J.P. Morgan and SBC Warburg were the joint lead managers.
It was followed by a 2.0 billion mark seven-year offering in March at a 370 b.p. spread over Bunds on which Credit Suisse First Boston and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell were the arrangers.

Kasyanov said Russia planned to sell part of the new issue in France after Moscow reached agreement with France last year about a settlement of Tsarist-era bonds held by French investors but not recognised by the former Soviet Union.
